note: Wave-2 graded items for class 12 Sociology pools (lesy201-208). One-term factual keys and numeric answers; machine-graded.

concepts.title: Colonialism as a Structure and System

questions.q: Colonialism under capitalism rewrote property law and dictated crops: far deeper than tribute or shallower?
Pre-capitalist conquerors took surplus and left what alone: the base economy or the army?
Whose rule rebuilt production itself in India: the British or the Mughals?
Production run by private owners for profit inside a market is called what?
A sovereign government over a defined territory with one citizenship is called a what?
Colonialism contradicted which of its own ideals in India: nationalism and democracy, or astronomy?
Industrialisation shifts production to machines run on what kind of energy: non-living or human?
Which Indian exports were ruined by Manchester goods: cotton and silk handicrafts or tea?
Colonial ruin of handicrafts pushed people back into what: agriculture or mining?
Britain was the first society to turn from rural to mainly what?
Colonial port cities sat on the coast to serve whose trade: the empire's or the monsoon's?
Through which port did most raw cotton move by 1900: Bombay or Madras?
Calcutta shipped jute; Madras sent coffee, sugar, indigo dyes and what fibre?
Assam tea gardens recruited workers through contractors, fraud and what kind of laws: penal or tax?

concepts.title: Rao's Three Types of Urban Impact

questions.q: M.S.A. Rao sorts village-urban contact into how many situations: three or thirty?
Migrant households over all households gives the migration what: rate or tax?
India's urban share climbed from about 17 percent in 1951 to about what by 2011: 31 or 3 percent?
Name Satish Saberwal's three faces of the modern context: communication, organisation and what else?
Reformers combined western liberalism with a fresh reading of what?
Which organisations let reformers campaign together: the Brahmo and Arya Samajes, or the East India Company?
Which Bengali body petitioned the British against the reformers: the Dharma Sabha or the Brahmo Samaj?
Who pushed anti-polygamy resolutions inside her own community: Jahanara Shah Nawas or Rammohun Roy?
Reform proposals split the very what they addressed: communities or rivers?
Who minted the term sanskritisation: M.N. Srinivas or Ghurye?
Sanskritisation works mostly inside which religious space: the Hindu or the Christian?
Where non-sanskritic castes dominate, what reverse pull operates: de-sanskritisation or westernisation?
Sanskritisation produces positional change, not what kind of change: structural or seasonal?
Westernisation names changes British rule produced across technology, institutions, ideology and what else?
The narrow sub-cultural kind of westernisation began with whom: intellectuals or farmers?
A home can fill with television and fridge yet hold what kind of views: conservative or reformed?
Modernisation widened into the claim that every society should follow which route of development: the West European or the African?
In the modern west, secularisation meant the fading hold of what?
In India, ritual still pursues secular ends such as what display: status or weather?
Caste has turned secular as caste associations and what kind of parties: caste-based or religious?

concepts.title: The Constitution as the Basic Norm

questions.q: A law bites because of what standing behind it: the state's means to compel, or public goodwill?
Justice is essentially about what: fairness or force?
Which court gives the final word on what the Constitution means: the Supreme Court or a district court?
The right to information was held part of free speech under which article: 19(1)(a) or 21?
Who imagined each village as a self-sufficient unit running its own affairs: Gandhi or Ambedkar?
Who feared village elites would capture local government: Ambedkar or Nehru?
Panchayats became constitutionally mandated bodies through which amendment: the 73rd or the 42nd?
What fraction of every local board is reserved for women: one third or one half?
Elections to panchayati raj bodies are compulsory every how many years: five or fifteen?
Panchayats levy and collect taxes, duties, tolls and what else: fees or votes?
Nyaya panchayats can impose what: fines or prison sentences?
Development duties of panchayats cover roads, wells, tanks, schools and what irrigation: minor or oceanic?
Gram sabhas often answer to a small coterie of whom: rich landlords or schoolchildren?
Reserved seats changed whose lives especially: Dalit women's or millionaires'?
Traditional caste panchayats took which kind of decisions: conservative or radical?
Meghalaya's tiered institutions belong to the Khasis, Jaintias and whom: the Garos or the Santhals?
Each Khasi clan keeps a durbar under its what: headman or president?
Who cautions that tradition is no guarantee of democracy: Tiplut Nongbri or Kalavati?

concepts.title: Parties, Interest Groups and Pressure Groups

questions.q: A body built to win lawful control of government through elections is called a what?
Interest groups pursue specific aims mainly by what: lobbying legislators or fighting elections?
Industrialists organise through FICCI and which other body: ASSOCHAM or INTUC?
Indian rural society is organised around which resource: land or silver?
Name the three agrarian ranks: landowners, tenant cultivators and whom else?
Ownership of land historically mapped onto which hierarchies: caste or alphabetical?
Which reform broke the old revenue-collecting class: abolition of zamindari or ceiling laws?
Ceiling laws were weakened by transfers of land among whom: relatives or strangers?
Tenants often lost what records of their cultivation: written or oral?
Which revolution raised foodgrain output in the 1960s: the Green Revolution or the White Revolution?
Which regions captured the Green Revolution gains: Punjab, Haryana and western UP, or Kerala, Goa and Assam?
questions.a: Punjab, Haryana and western Uttar Pradesh

questions.q: Green Revolution irrigation lowered which tables: water or price?
Newly prosperous farmers turned economic strength into what: political clout or pilgrimage?
Rural diversification ran into dairying and what else: horticulture or mining?
What kind of farming spread after reform: contract or monastic?
Workers migrating seasonally while keeping family in the village show the circulation of what: labour or money?
Employers prefer circulating workers because they can be paid what: less or more?
The village bears the cost of raising and schooling whose labour: the city's workers or officials'?
From which year did liberalisation reach the countryside: 1991 or 1947?
Agrarian distress grew into one of the period's central what: social problems or celebrations?
Globalisation exposed farmers to world price swings and what kind of agribusiness: corporate or village?
Marx named the condition of workers who never see the finished good: what is it?
A factory breaks production into many narrow what: steps or miracles?
What share of Indian workers did farming hold in 2018-19: 42.5 percent or 4.25?
Which sector now produces more than half of growth: services or farming?
About what share of Indian workers are self-employed: over half or a tenth?
Regular salaried work covers about what percent of workers: 24 or 80?
The organised sector covers registered units employing how many or more people: ten or two?
Over nine-tenths of Indian work sits in which sector: informal or organised?
The government selling its stake in public companies is called what?
Which company was the first privatised: Modern Foods or Tata Steel?
In Kanpur's mills, the jobber drawn from the workers' own region was called the what: mistri or munim?
Almost everyone finds industrial jobs through what: personal contacts or advertisements?
On a car assembly line, what sets the tempo: the machine or the worker?
At Maruti Udyog, how many minutes of rest does a worker get in a whole day: forty-five or four?
Which act of 1952 laid down safety rules for mines: the Mines Act or the Factories Act?
Many underground miners develop which disease: silicosis or myopia?

concepts.title: Home-Based Work and the Bidi Chain

questions.q: Bidi and lace workers are paid by the what: piece or month?
A tendu-leaf collector gathers about how many bundles a day: a hundred or ten?
The employer's counter of shutting the gate is called a what: lockout or strike?
Who led the 1982 Bombay textile strike: Datta Samant or Gandhi?
From which month did India withdraw quantitative restrictions on imports: April 2001 or April 1991?
Globalisation hands new chances to some and what to others: losses or prizes?
Which ancient route joined India to China, Persia, Egypt and Rome: the Silk Route or the Grand Trunk Road?
Amartya Sen retells which parable against suspicion of the outside world: the well-frog or the blind men?
From which month did liberalisation open the Indian economy: July 1991 or January 1950?
IMF loans came with conditions imposing what: structural adjustment or a festival?

concepts.title: TNCs and the New Division of Labour

questions.q: Corporations producing in more than one country are called what: transnational or national?
Nike's shoe output moved on to which two countries in the 1990s: Thailand and Indonesia, or France and Italy?
Of the Pontiac Le Mans price of 20,000 dollars, how many dollars stay with Americans: 7,600 or 19,000?
Which country took 48 percent of the overseas share for labour and assembly: South Korea or Germany?
Which city is India's financial capital: Mumbai or Patna?
The economy whose products are based in information is called what: weightless or weighty?
In 1998, the USA and Canada held what percent of world internet users: 62 or 6?
In 2017-18, about what share of Indian households had internet connections: a quarter or nine-tenths?
At independence India had how many telephone lines: 84,000 or 84 million?
What are roadside call booths called: PCOs or ATMs?
Blending the global with the local is called what: glocalisation or isolation?
McDonald's drops which meat in India: beef or chicken?
Since the 1970s, city growth's engine has shifted from factories to what consumption: cultural or industrial?
Which game show fed overnight-fortune dreams: Kaun Banega Crorepati or Antakshari?

concepts.title: Craft and Knowledge Systems Under Threat

questions.q: Which traditions have multinationals tried to patent: tulsi, haldi and basmati, or cycles and cars?
About how many theatre groups died with Mumbai's mill districts: thirty or three?
Post-socialist globalisation wore which face: neo-liberal or neo-baroque?
Which intergovernmental body increasingly shapes the rules of trade: the WTO or the WHO?
Between 2003 and 2004, how many jobs did Asia-Pacific add: 25 million or 250 million?
Job growth of 1.6 percent trailed economic growth of over what: 7 percent or 70 percent?

concepts.title: Mass Media as a Social Institution

questions.q: Mass communication needs big capital, production plants and what: management or luck?
Which two forces dominate mass media: the state and the market, or villages and temples?
Who invented the printing press around 1440: Johann Gutenberg or Yi Jing?
Benedict Anderson called the nation an imagined what: community or village?
Which prime minister wanted the free press as democracy's watchdog: Jawaharlal Nehru or Indira Gandhi?
Which crisis brought hourly radio news from 6 am to midnight: the 1971 Bangladesh crisis or the 1962 war?
At independence India had how many radio stations: six or sixty?
Which 1960s device made radio sets mobile and cheap: the transistor or the valve?

concepts.title: Television from SITE to the Epics

questions.q: SITE beamed programmes to how many community sets: 2,400 or 24?
Colour transmission arrived with which 1982 event: the Asian Games or the World Cup?
Which two private broadcasters arrived in 1991-92: Star TV and Zee TV, or Doordarshan and AIR?
India holds the world's which largest TV market: second or tenth?
Cable operators grew from 100 in 1984 to about how many by 1999: 60,000 or 600?
In which two cities were apartment buildings first wired for cable: Mumbai and Ahmedabad, or Delhi and Jaipur?
Indian language papers grew fastest in which three languages: Hindi, Telugu and Kannada, or Tamil, Urdu and English?
Average daily circulation rose from 39.1 million copies in 2006 to what in 2016: 62.8 million or 6.28 million?

concepts.title: Hindi Belt Migration and Delhi's Market

questions.q: What percent of Delhi's population came from the Hindi belt: 52 or 15?
The Hindustan's Delhi edition leapt from 64,000 copies in 2003 to how many by 2005: 425,000 or 4,250?
Which war popularised CNN in 1991: the Gulf War or the Kargil War?
Sony began in India with how many Hindi films a week: ten or a hundred?
A blend of information and entertainment is called what?
The live rescue of which trapped child split opinion on voyeurism: Little Prince or Little Master?
Privately owned FM stations were allowed from which year: 2002 or 1992?
Radio Mirchi belongs to which group: the Times of India group or the Star network?
Collective action kept up over time with organisation and shared ideology is called a social what?
Because change threatens entrenched interests, what rise in defence: counter movements or festivals?
Over 1.25 million people signed the People's Charter in which year: 1839 or 1939?
In which year did all men over 21 gain the vote in Britain: 1918 or 1818?
Which revolution toppled a monarchy in the name of liberty, equality and fraternity: the French or the Industrial?
Who showed that crowds acted on a shared moral economy: E.P. Thompson or Janis?
Which movement type seeks a change in members' personal consciousness: redemptive or reformist?
Which movement type aims at total change of state and structure: revolutionary or reformist?
New movements centre on quality of life and identity rather than what: class and power reorganisation, or fashion?
Who tied India's 1970s surge of movements to disgust with parliamentary democracy: Rajni Kothari or Andre Beteille?
Which movement saw villagers hug trees to stop contractors felling them: Chipko or Narmada?
Who described Chipko in the book Unquiet Woods: Ramachandra Guha or M.N. Srinivas?
Which satyagraha of 1917-18 fought indigo plantations: Champaran or Bardoli?
The Tebhaga movement demanded what share of the produce for sharecroppers: two thirds or one fourth?
Raising the sharecropper's share from one half to two thirds adds what fraction of the crop: one sixth or one half?
That gain measured against the old half share is a what percent improvement: thirty-three and a third, or three?
New farmers' movement members are market-involved what: commodity producers or subsistence peasants?
The new farmers' ideology ran anti-state and anti-what: urban or anti-education?
India's factories rose from the early 1860s in which port towns: Calcutta and Bombay, or Delhi and Kanpur?
About how many strikes hit the Bombay textile mills in September-October 1917: 30 or 300?
The Dalit movement is at bottom a struggle to be what: touched or taxed?
The word Dalit was revived in which decade: the early 1970s or the 1930s?
The label backward classes spread from Madras presidency from which year: 1872 or 1972?
In politics, caste shed its ritual content and became what: secularised or sacred?
Whose uprising made him the icon of the Jharkhand movement: Birsa Munda or Sidhu?
Adivasis united in hatred of whom: the dikus, meaning migrant traders and moneylenders, or priests?
The Women's India Association was founded in which year: 1917 or 1971?
The women's movement renewed in which period: the mid-1970s or the 1950s?
